name: Special right triangles
whenToUse: Any figure with a square's diagonal, an equilateral triangle's altitude, a regular hexagon, or a $30^\circ$, $45^\circ$ or $60^\circ$ angle in a right triangle.
example: An equilateral triangle with side $10$ splits into two $30$-$60$-$90$ triangles with hypotenuse $10$ and short leg $5$, so its altitude is $5\sqrt{3}$ and its area is $25\sqrt{3}$.
pitfall: In the $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the side opposite $30^\circ$ is the shortest and the $\sqrt{3}$ side is opposite $60^\circ$. Do not swap them.
